rules: A comparator mismatch is allowed only when an exact stage-scoped entry has status approved.
An open_debt or pending_evidence entry gives a known failure an ID but never turns it into a pass.
A resolved entry preserves the audit trail but is never assigned to a current finding and never suppresses a recurrence.
An unregistered mismatch is a hard failure.
An entry with stale reference evidence cannot suppress a mismatch.
kind=upstream_backport identifies an approved fix taken from the exact upstream_commits, not a Polygrad-specific policy; it grants no additional mismatch allowance.

Close an upstream_backport only after verifying that the new pin contains its fixes and the affected parity/regression checks pass. A release number alone is insufficient; retain regression tests after closure.
Wasm renderer-local independent-lane SIMD packing preserves shared graphs and reduction order; it grants no numeric mismatch allowance.

entries.area: Bound single-use WGSL expression inlining for parser capacity
entries.tinygrad: Pinned 6f87158d and upstream c10034fc2 inline eligible single-use expressions without a WGSL complexity bound. A 1024-term Boolean OR chain exceeds Chrome 155 expression depth 512 in both.
entries.polygrad: Use pinned inlining and declaration placement, but materialize an eligible expression at its existing linearized position when its emitted syntax punctuation count exceeds 128. Count operators as well as delimiters because associative formatting can flatten a DAG into a long parser chain. Other backends, graph structure, arithmetic and execution order are unchanged.
entries.rationale: The full browser ONNX computed-scatter fixture reaches this parser limit. A render-local temporary bounds expression growth without disabling normal inlining or changing the optimizer.
entries.approval: User instructed proceed with fixes, measure, then evaluate pinned and latest Tinygrad on 2026-10-26 after the reported stop requiring bounded WGSL inlining and symbolic BITCAST evaluation.
entries.close_when: The reference bounds WGSL expressions sufficiently for the browser parser. Recheck long associative and unary chains, computed scatter, ordinary shader identity and browser values before removing this exception.

entries.area: Reject ungated shared stores with omitted nontrivial local axes
entries.tinygrad: Pinned 6f87158d and inspected upstream d16046fb guard missing local axes only on GLOBAL stores. Explicit options or BEAM can give independent reductions separate local axes and emit ungated LOCAL stores with duplicate concurrent writers.
entries.polygrad: At GPU-dimension lowering, reject an ungated LOCAL store when a local axis with maximum extent greater than one is absent from its INDEX ranges. Report the axis and extent before shader emission. Singleton axes, fully addressed stores, GLOBAL/private storage and pre-existing STORE predicates retain their existing handling. The coalescer is unchanged. A GPU-only BEAM cache-key revision excludes pre-policy winners; CPU cache identity and public ABI are unchanged.
entries.rationale: Fail closed on the reproduced duplicate-writer schedules instead of changing store predicates, reduction order or coalescer admission. Fresh BEAM search skips rejected compilations before timing. Explicit options fail with an error. This is a narrow admission check, not a general proof of address injectivity or predicate correctness. It adds no lane sharing, heuristic changes, automatic schedule fallback, or numeric mismatch allowance.
entries.approval: User instructed "investigate further and fix" on 2026-10-25 after review recommending scoped schedule rejection with cache handling. This replaces the unapproved writer-election/coalescing proposal; no approval for lane sharing or default heuristic changes is inferred.
entries.close_when: The reference rejects these duplicate shared-writer schedules or emits race-free equivalents. Revalidate explicit options, BEAM cache migration, accepted shader identity and affected backend/frontend gates before closing. No scheduling or arithmetic divergence beyond rejection is permitted.

entries.area: Boolean repeated-product reduction preserves result dtype
entries.tinygrad: Pinned reduce_unparented replaces unparented MUL ranges with POW(value, weakint_count), promoting a Boolean reduction result to weakint and failing downstream Boolean UOp verification.
entries.polygrad: Only for REDUCE MUL with Boolean result dtype, each removed range becomes WHERE(count == 0, bool true, value). Nonempty Boolean products are idempotent; any empty removed range returns the Boolean multiplicative identity. Parent-dependent ranges stay in the retained reduction. Other reduction operators and numeric result dtypes keep the pinned rule and original exact count.
entries.rationale: Preserve Boolean all() semantics for broadcast values, symbolic nonnegative counts and empty products without frontend workarounds or changes to numeric accumulation.
entries.approval: User approved the narrowly scoped fix on 2026-10-22, requiring symbolic-zero/multiple-empty-range coverage, applicable unfiltered gates and a commit separate from atan.
entries.close_when: The pin preserves Boolean repeated products, including symbolic zero and multiple removed ranges with an empty range. Rerun graph/type, value and frontend regressions before removing this narrow codegen divergence; no Tensor/autograd graph mismatch is allowed.

entries.tinygrad: Pinned atan uses asin(x/sqrt(1+x*x)); x*x overflows and the asin approximation limits value and derivative accuracy.
entries.polygrad: Uses masked reciprocal and pi/4 reductions followed by dtype-specific alternating polynomials; preserves signed zero and differentiates the same graph.
entries.rationale: Probability tails require accurate values and gradients. This approved departure changes only atan, not asin or acos; exact graph pairs bound the allowance.
entries.approval: User approved the scoped atan accuracy departure on 2026-10-22, conditional on signed-zero preservation, dtype-specific boundary neighbors and completed C sanitizer validation.
entries.close_when: Recheck against a future reference with accurate atan; retain signed-zero, value, derivative and reload regressions.

entries.tinygrad: Pinned memory_coalescing requires an offset divisible by vector length, except on DSP where must_divide=False.
entries.polygrad: Uses the same exemption for Wasm ordinary vector loads/stores. Existing width and dtype limits remain; only contiguous accesses to the same storage with the same predicate are grouped. CPU, X86, WebGPU and other target policies are unchanged.
entries.rationale: Wasm ordinary SIMD memory operations permit unaligned addresses. Requiring vector alignment needlessly scalarizes odd-stride kernels. This changes lowered memory grouping, not accessed elements, masks, arithmetic order or numerical tolerances; it does not apply to atomic accesses.
entries.approval: User explicitly approved Wasm-only unaligned coalescing on 2026-10-19, with alignment/bounds regressions and affected gates.
entries.close_when: The pinned lowering supports Wasm unaligned vector memory coalescing, or an equivalent target capability removes this difference; retain access, mask, bounds and value regressions.

entries.area: Default Wasm specialized matmul and row-reduction numerical order
entries.tinygrad: Shared reduce_ranges_to_acc and expand_horizontal_reduce define the optimized accumulator graph; divisible generic Wasm probes add four-term groups into one scalar accumulator.
entries.polygrad: Both scheduled-SINK renderer specializers and the relaxed matmul compile retry are removed. Every Wasm program now crosses shared optimization and generic rendering. Custom matmuls are selected before lowering under PG-DIV-012, not rediscovered in the renderer.
entries.rationale: The previous matmul and striped row-reduction paths bypassed shared optimization. Their deletion removes this hidden policy; production row reductions retain the pinned grouped/scalar orders, tested with varying and cancellation inputs. Target-level SIMD packing remains separate.

resolution.evidence: Specialized emitters, detectors and declarations removed; public lowering matches generic reduction topology and exact varying/cancellation outputs. C Wasm suite: 105 passed, zero failures. This historical row grants no numeric allowance.

entries.area: HIP automatic tensor-core wave capability guard
entries.tinygrad: Pinned HIPRenderer selects an AMD tensor-core table from the architecture string without checking the executing device's wave size.
entries.polygrad: Disables automatic tensor-core selection when the selected template's thread count differs from the detected hardware wave size; ordinary matmul lowering remains available. Explicit WMMA instructions are unchanged.
entries.rationale: A tensor-core lane layout must match the executing wave. This backend-only fallback grants no tensor, logical, physical, or numerical mismatch allowance.
entries.approval: User approved the tested wave-size capability guard on 2026-10-15.
entries.close_when: The pinned backend rejects incompatible tensor-core layouts before automatic selection; rerun topology and value probes before removing this allowance.

entries.tinygrad: Pinned erf uses the A&S polynomial, with a roughly 1.4e-7 FP64 absolute-error floor; the later upstream sign repair fixes its center derivative but not its accuracy.
entries.polygrad: Uses the Cephes central rational and complementary-tail approximations in shared C graph construction, also consumed by exact GELU. Computes low-precision inputs in float32 and casts back. No renderer, compiler or autograd rule changes.
entries.rationale: Probability calculations need FP64 accuracy and a differentiable center. The related erfc, erfinv, ndtri, lgamma and digamma APIs are Polygrad additions, not pinned methods.
entries.approval: User approved a proved, documented erf accuracy improvement for Polyprob on 2026-10-13.
evidence: js/test/test_tensor.js:core probability special functions and higher derivatives
entries.close_when: The pinned reference adopts an equivalently accurate differentiable erf construction; recheck complete graph pairs before removing this allowance.

entries.area: retained logical and explicit placement capability
entries.tinygrad: Tensor owns one mutable, deviceful Tensor.uop
entries.polygrad: Default uop_physical is eagerly constructed in C and must match tinygrad Tensor.uop; Polygrad may additionally retain a deviceless logical graph and physical template for Model, export, and explicit place outside default realization. Portable BUFFER(UNIQUE) graphs preserve CONTIGUOUS requests until placement; unlike storage-free expressions, absence of a device does not make them virtual.
entries.rationale: Portable logical retention, export, explicit placement, and PolyModel capture are approved Polygrad superset capabilities; default physical construction and execution are parity surfaces.
entries.approval: AGENTS.md Core Invariants and user-approved logical/physical split

entries.tinygrad: No language-neutral ABI package equivalent; symbolic SHRINK has no call-time bounds admission. Transformer sampling advances global Tensor RNG, outside state_dict.
entries.polygrad: PolyModel owns named bindings, entrypoints, objectives, and package metadata. Call admission derives SHRINK bounds for reads and writes from each entrypoint graph, before input/state mutation. Sampling and captured training RNG are ordinary Model AUX state: reset preserves progress and bundles checkpoint it.
entries.rationale: Model-only safety and portable state extend the product contract without changing ordinary Tensor or TinyJit semantics. Derived view admission is not a sandbox for arbitrary graph programs.
entries.approval: AGENTS.md Core Invariants; user-approved Model read/write bounds and persistent sampling RNG, 2026-09-23

entries.tinygrad: Python Buffer objects own runtime storage
entries.polygrad: PolyCtx owns ctx->buffers residency keyed by BUFFER UOps
entries.rationale: The C ABI requires explicit context-owned residency while preserving tinygrad graph semantics.
entries.approval: AGENTS.md Core Invariants

entries.tinygrad: PROGRAM may carry SOURCE and BINARY children
entries.polygrad: PROGRAM carries source/program metadata while driver and compiled-binary payloads remain in private runtime-cache entries
entries.rationale: Non-serializable C driver resources are kept outside the immutable UOp arena.
entries.approval: ARCHITECTURE.md Scheduling
entries.close_when: Revisit only if immutable serializable BINARY bytes become a product requirement.

entries.tinygrad: No language-neutral Polygrad bundle equivalent
entries.polygrad: IR, bundle, safetensors, and named Model export/import
entries.rationale: Portable packaging is an intentional Polygrad superset feature.
entries.approval: project architecture

entries.tinygrad: Pinned two-i32 lowering fails for dynamic uint32 shift counts and signed SHR
entries.polygrad: Two-i32 lowering preserves valid dynamic counts and arithmetic signed SHR, plus the existing raw-C i32,i32 to i64 superset case
entries.rationale: This is a correctness-preserving backend superset over a pinned tinygrad failure.
entries.approval: documented backend divergence
entries.close_when: Re-evaluate when the pinned tinygrad behavior changes.

entries.tinygrad: Python GC and weak references own Tensor/UOp wrapper lifetime
entries.polygrad: C arenas and explicit frontend owner hooks own core objects
entries.rationale: C object ownership cannot be identical to Python GC; semantic graph lifetime must still satisfy the parity and capture gates.
entries.approval: project architecture

entries.tinygrad: Pinned WGSLRenderer maps int8/uint8/int16/uint16 CAST and ALU results to untruncated i32/u32 registers; widening can expose overflow bits.
entries.polygrad: WGSL masks unsigned and sign-extends signed 8/16-bit CAST and ALU results before widening, following dtype.truncate and PythonProgram. Float-to-narrow conversion stages through signed i32 so negatives can wrap. Ordinary float conversion range rules, Tensor graphs and packed storage layout are unchanged.
entries.rationale: A paired shader execution reproduces lost int8 narrowing in both renderers. Correct typed values fix uint8 Tensor-weight lerp without a Tensor-level workaround. Wasm uses the same typed-value contract; native C integer expression promotion remains a separately observed pinned backend behavior.
entries.approval: User 2026-09-07: fix the identified bug and document divergences, including source comments.
evidence: js/test/test_tensor.js:pointwise owners: narrow integer casts survive widening
entries.close_when: Re-evaluate against the same typed cast/ALU probes when the Tinygrad pin changes. This row grants no Tensor or physical graph allowance.

entries.area: shared dense Llama factory and scaled rotary tables
entries.tinygrad: Pinned extra/models/llama.py supplies dense Llama construction and unscaled RoPE; its HF converter permutes half-split Q/K weights into interleaved layout.
entries.polygrad: A C-owned Model factory uses existing RMSNorm/SDPA/SwiGLU and half-split poly_tensor_rope directly on HF weights. Optional llama3 wavelength scaling follows Meta/Hugging Face, and tied names share Model storage.
entries.rationale: One configuration/checkpoint must construct the same model from C, Python, Node and Wasm. No compiler, Tensor, scheduler or physical-graph allowance is granted by this model-layer extension.
entries.approval: User 2026-09-16 requested the shared Llama port and explicitly selected both Llama 2 and Llama 3.x.
entries.close_when: Re-evaluate model construction and rotary references on pin changes; this row never excuses core mismatches.

entries.area: invalid padded integer division and remainder
entries.tinygrad: Pinned rangeify can evaluate integer division/remainder of masked zero loads before discarding the invalid result; CPU MOD/cumsum at extent 10 raises SIGFPE with nonzero input divisors.
entries.polygrad: Indexing and STAGE fusion guard integer IDIV/MOD/FLOORDIV/FLOORMOD denominators with WHERE(coordinate_valid, original_divisor, typed_one) before backend lowering. Valid coordinates, including real zero divisors, are unchanged.
entries.rationale: Invalid padded coordinates must not trap while evaluating a result that will be discarded. This grants no Tensor graph, valid-coordinate arithmetic, or general division-by-zero allowance.
entries.approval: User 2026-09-17: approve guarded padded coordinates, at the shared coordinate-validity boundary.
entries.close_when: Re-evaluate the exact invalid-coordinate graph and execution probes on Tinygrad pin changes. No backend-specific arithmetic policy is introduced.

entries.area: portable CLIP, ViT, DINOv2 and DINOv3 vision models
entries.tinygrad: Pinned extra/models/clip.py and vit.py implement CLIP/ViT authoring. The pin has no DINOv2 or DINOv3 model implementation.
entries.polygrad: Shared C registry builders expose fixed-resolution eval Models and HF checkpoint imports. CLIP/ViT reuse pinned components with HF names, activations and pooling; DINOv2/v3 follow Transformers5.3.0. DINOv3 precomputes fixed-position 2D rotary AUX. Tensor, compiler and execution semantics are unchanged.
entries.rationale: The user requested all four models as portability checks across Python, JavaScript, native and Wasm execution. This is a Model construction extension, not a physical-graph parity allowance.
entries.approval: User 2026-09-18: create CLIP and DINO, explicitly DINO2 and DINO3, then include ViT as a portability check.
entries.close_when: Re-evaluate authoring references when the Tinygrad or Transformers reference changes. This row never excuses compiler, Tensor or backend mismatches.

entries.area: Physical UOp GEMM providers; Wasm default, other backends opt-in
entries.tinygrad: Pinned llm/kernels/amd.py selects UOp-authored custom kernels for supported AMD quantized Linear inputs; it has no equivalent FP32 AVX2 matmul kernel.
entries.polygrad: POLY_KERNELS=1 selects fixed-shape FP32 broadcast matmuls and rank-three autograd contractions on native AVX2/FMA CPUs before decomposition, including resolved ordinary FUNCTION bodies. A 4x24 UOp kernel consumes scheduled panel packing; unsupported cases fall back. Existing CPU workers receive even output-tile-axis slices, using the pin's thread-count candidates and work floor; each output retains serial K accumulation. On the same opt-in path, a last-axis normalized exponential feeding matmul is materialized once when its fixed FP32 table is at most 32 MiB and reused across output columns. Authoring and portable logical graphs remain unchanged. Serial FMA accumulation and physical materialization can round differently from generic reductions.
entries.rationale: The Wasm path replaces the packed 4x8 provider with one no-pack UOp provider, selected before fusion. Fixed FP32 M<=512 and K,N<=4096 with a shared right operand are supported. Contiguous K rows use four K%4 accumulators, combined (s0+s2)+(s1+s3); contiguous output columns use serial K accumulation through the shared GEMM builder. Both use separate strict multiply/add. Fixed tails preserve those orders, and output-column prefix/tail CALLs write disjoint views of one buffer without packing. The striped order can improve or worsen cancellation error: [2^25,-2^25,1,0,...] gives0 versus serial1; swapping the middle terms reverses which order loses1. Tests pin the orders, repeated results and binary64 errors; no promise of being no worse than serial is made. With POLY_KERNELS unset, only Wasm GEMM selection is enabled by default. kernels=false or POLY_KERNELS=0 disables selection; kernels=true or POLY_KERNELS=1 enables all supported providers. CPU, WebGPU and interval-sum providers retain explicit opt-in. Matmul outputs are materialized before epilogues, so realize-stage dispatch counts can differ. Both renderer specializers and the relaxed multiply-add retry are removed; disabled/unsupported operations use shared optimization and generic rendering. WebGPU uses32x64 workgroup tiles and serial K, with no packing dispatch. Unsupported cases fall back. Authoring, gradients and portable bundles retain generic operations. Policy locks at first lowering. No persistent packed-state cache, host-dependent relaxed arithmetic or new executor is introduced.
entries.approval: User 2026-09-25: proceed with guarded physical custom-kernel integration and attention materialization. User 2026-09-26: proceed to Wasm and WebGPU kernels. User approved the strict four-partial-sum opt-in replacement and subsequent explicit cancellation tradeoff qualification; default enablement remains a separate decision. User 2026-10-21 explicitly superseded default-off: enable Wasm UOp matmuls by default and remove both renderer specializers; all other operations use plain rendering plus optimizer options. This approves physical selection, realize-stage materialization and the documented strict reduction order, not a universal speedup.
entries.close_when: Re-evaluate numerical error, selection and matched performance before expanding supported shapes or enabling other providers by default. This allowance covers physical matmul selection/materialization and documented accumulation order, not authoring, differentiation or portable-export mismatches.

entries.area: Full-range float64 sine decomposition; Wasm nontrapping casts
entries.tinygrad: Pinned ClangRenderer decomposes f64 SIN using a Payne-Hanek reduction with a 32-bit mantissa and a bounded 2/pi table. Out-of-range float-to-integer casts have backend-dependent results.
entries.polygrad: Shared f64 SIN decomposition retains all 53 significand bits and uses a 1280-bit 2/pi table with integer quadrant/remainder extraction. Values below one use the existing sine polynomial directly; larger values use the integer reduction, avoiding cancellation and reassociation of split-pi subtraction. f16/f32 decomposition and portable authoring graphs remain unchanged. Cosine remains the pinned sin(pi/2-x) composition and retains its subtraction-rounding limitation. Wasm scalar float-to-integer conversions saturate, with NaN becoming zero, matching its SIMD casts rather than trapping in unused WHERE branches.
entries.rationale: Fix the inherited float64 range-reduction defect in the shared arithmetic graph rather than bypassing it with backend-native sine. Saturating Wasm casts prevent module traps for eagerly evaluated discarded values; narrow integer conversions retain signed staging and width masking.
entries.approval: User 2026-09-28 explicitly requests fixing shared decomposition instead of native float64 sine substitution; also requests CUDA retention and Wasm cast fixes.

entries.area: Bicubic interpolation for checkpoint-preserving vision resolution selection
entries.tinygrad: Pinned OpMixin.interpolate supports linear, nearest and nearest-exact, and rejects bicubic.
entries.polygrad: The C Tensor interpolation API additionally supports separable bicubic interpolation of two fixed spatial dimensions, with a=-0.75, replicated edge samples, optional align_corners and no antialiasing. Tensor interpolation and ONNX Resize share an axis sampler with configurable coefficient and outside-sample exclusion; callers retain coordinate policies. Cubic weights use fractional-coordinate Horner polynomials rather than the pin's distance-based evaluation. DINOv2 input_image_size specializes the input while retaining original checkpoint position parameters and composing their interpolation in the portable graph.
entries.rationale: Support original DINOv2 checkpoints at their processor's input resolution without app-specific weight conversion. Existing interpolation modes and IR vocabulary are unchanged; frontends delegate to C.
entries.approval: User 2026-10-02 approves expanding Polygrad primitives for DINO and requests fixing library gaps rather than demo workarounds.

entries.tinygrad: flatten_range and do_split_ends collect the transitive active ranges of every operand, so END(inner) also ends outer when inner's bound depends on outer.
entries.polygrad: Explicit RANGE operands name only that range. Non-RANGE integer expressions still expand to their active ranges; boolean and void backedges are preserved rather than expanded into loop operands.
entries.rationale: Preserve UOp._ranges semantics for data-dependent nested reductions, including segmented sums. Closing the outer range prematurely creates invalid control flow. No new IR operation or Tensor topology allowance.
entries.approval: User 2026-10-04 says proceed after reviewing the reproduced inherited bug and proposed compiler correction.
entries.close_when: Pinned tinygrad preserves explicit dependent range closeout with equivalent nested-loop tests.

entries.tinygrad: Pinned Tensor graphs express interval sums with comparisons, WHERE and REDUCE; generic lowering visits the masked reduction domain.
entries.polygrad: With kernels=true, recognize fixed FP32 [1,N,W] values masked by int32 [S,1,1] lower/upper bounds and the canonical arange(N), then summed over N. An existing-UOp CALL kernel reads only the intersection of each interval with [0,N). Empty or reversed intervals return zero; arbitrary, overlapping and out-of-range bounds retain the mask's semantics. Each output accumulates serially, which can round differently from generic reduction trees. Shapes outside the conservative matcher and unsupported targets retain generic lowering.
entries.rationale: Remove repeated scan dispatches for grouped sparse reductions without a new IR op, executor, public tensor API or opaque authoring graph. Autograd and portable exports continue to contain ordinary Tensor operations; kernels=false retains that graph. No default numerical-parity allowance.
entries.approval: User 2026-10-04 requests implementing a general segmented reduction and subsequently says go after the dependent-loop compiler correction.
entries.close_when: Revisit after pinned tinygrad provides equivalent optional interval reduction lowering.

entries.tinygrad: Pinned Tensor.linear_with_vars publishes the buffer map before execution. Errors do not restore Tensor roots, so retry can read unwritten storage.
entries.polygrad: Retain exact affected Tensor roots through execution and restore them on failure. Compilation/runtime preparation before the first application write is retryable. After a partial execution, output storage of attempted calls is invalidated, including aliases; untouched calls and read-only inputs are not invalidated. No rollback of bytes or allowance for successful graph/value differences.
entries.rationale: Prevent silently wrong retry values while preserving valid weights on preparation failures. Backend runtime construction is lazy and may fail between dispatches, so the failure boundary follows attempted writes, not the name compile_linear.
entries.approval: User 2026-10-05 says go after reviewing exact-root rollback before writes and separate handling of partial execution.
entries.close_when: Pinned tinygrad provides equivalent failure recovery.

entries.tinygrad: Pinned tanh is 2*sigmoid(2*x)-1, which loses relative accuracy near zero and rounds sufficiently small nonzero inputs to zero.
entries.polygrad: Use an odd polynomial for |x|<1/4 and (1-exp(-2*abs(x)))/(1+exp(-2*abs(x))) elsewhere, with bounded intermediates. Compute low-precision inputs in float32. This changes tanh graphs, their derivatives and composites using tanh (including GELU and recurrent layers), without adding an IR operation or backend-specific implementation.
entries.rationale: Audio attention softcapping exposes cancellation in small logits. Fix the shared Tensor operation rather than changing model math or loosening reference checks.
entries.approval: User 2026-10-07: Fix shared tanh now, in response to an explicit request for regression tests and a documented tinygrad divergence.
entries.close_when: Pinned tinygrad supplies a cancellation-free tanh with equivalent numerical coverage.

entries.tinygrad: Pinned ONNX runner has no Loop implementation.
entries.polygrad: Unroll Loop at import only when trip count and each evaluated condition are closed constant graphs. Carry fixed-shape tensors through scoped subgraphs, bounded by the existing node/value budgets and a 4096-iteration guard. Reject data-dependent control and scan outputs. Execute the resulting ordinary Model through existing Tensor/compiler/runtime paths.
entries.rationale: Supports statically terminating exported model programs without a second executor or observing runtime inputs during import.
entries.approval: User 2026-10-09: Yes, add bounded static Loop support.
entries.close_when: Revisit when pinned tinygrad implements Loop. This grants no Tensor, compiler or runtime parity mismatch.

entries.area: constant unique ONNX ScatterND overwrite indices
entries.tinygrad: Pinned ONNX runner updates one axis-0 slice at a time through tensor indexing.
entries.polygrad: For closed constant, unique indices and concrete import-time shapes with reduction=none, precompute one int32 source map with -1 for untouched destinations. Gather update slices and select against the original data. Dynamic indices, duplicates, reductions and maps outside the import budget keep the existing lowering. Unresolved dimensions remain rejected by ONNX shape admission.
entries.rationale: Avoid Cartesian boolean masks whose repeated substitution exceeds the browser memory budget. No Tensor operation or compiler rewrite changes; source-map storage is retained in the portable Model.
entries.approval: User 2026-10-09 approved option 1 with conditions: verify indexed-load collapse, one int32 map, closed unique reduction-free indices, differential/fallback tests, decoder ORT and memory checks, and an importer-only divergence.
entries.close_when: Pinned ONNX lowering supports equivalent compact constant scatter maps. This grants no Tensor, compiler or runtime parity mismatch.

entries.tinygrad: Pinned ONNX runner updates one axis-0 slice at a time through tensor indexing; it does not recognize Cartesian index expressions.
entries.polygrad: Track closed int64 Range expressions through supported singleton reshapes, expansion, slicing and concatenation. Prove unique, in-bounds Cartesian overwrite coordinates and lower them with permutation, flip, reshape, padding and WHERE. Try this before source maps. Computed irregular index readbacks above 64 KiB skip the map path; stored indices retain the aggregate import budget. Other cases keep the existing lowering.
entries.rationale: Avoid both expanded host index computation and persistent source-map storage for regular writes. Materialize the complete WHERE output so a following reduction does not repeat activation/dilation/select work. No Tensor semantics or compiler rules change.
entries.approval: User 2026-10-10 approved collector work followed by grid recognition, a map-path evaluation budget, differential tests and an importer divergence next to PG-DIV-020.
entries.close_when: Pinned ONNX lowering recognizes equivalent regular index grids without enumerating their elements. This grants no Tensor, compiler or runtime parity mismatch.

entries.area: opt-in BEAM timing and final heuristic comparison
entries.tinygrad: Pinned v0.14.0 selects the BEAM winner without comparing the default heuristic. Earlier BEAM_COMPARE performed full-size cache-cleared comparisons; c77cb57454c5b6cede8426cdeeeed7eef4b5b9fc removed it as untested.
entries.polygrad: When BEAM is enabled, compare its winner with the ordinary schedule using alternating full-size measurements. WebGPU search and comparison calibrate queued samples toward 4 ms, capped at 128 dispatches, rotating scratch storage toward 32 MiB with at most 16 banks to reduce idle-clock and small-matrix cache bias. Reject a selected winner when both final candidates fail execution. Cache the selected options with the timing-policy version. BEAM_COMPARE=0 restores pinned timing and selection; both disk and runtime caches distinguish the policy.
entries.rationale: Search can choose a slower kernel than the default. Final comparison guards against measured regressions without changing BEAM=0 compilation. Timing noise still prevents an absolute performance guarantee.
entries.approval: User 2026-10-10 explicitly requested adding the heuristic comparison and investigating historical BEAM_COMPARE; 2026-10-11 requested adaptive queued search timing with rotating scratch storage.
entries.close_when: The pinned reference adopts equivalent final comparison; this allowance affects only BEAM-enabled schedule selection.

entries.area: assignment of resident data into an unrealized expression
entries.tinygrad: replace_store_after_with_contig calls src.contiguous(tag=u.tag). With a resident multidimensional array source this can drop assignment provenance: realize returns without publishing destination storage and readback fails with must be BUFFER Ops.ADD. The simple one-dimensional control succeeds.
entries.polygrad: Materialize the synthetic assignment CONTIGUOUS even when its source already has storage. Publish independent destination storage under the original assignment tag. Ordinary contiguous on resident tensors remains a no-op; realized assignment targets retain their existing storage.
entries.rationale: Parameter initialization must leave a readable value without making later source or destination writes alias. The defect is shared with the pin, not an allocation-only porting difference.
entries.approval: User 2026-10-11: Fix and document the shared defect.
entries.close_when: The pinned reference preserves assignment provenance and independent destination storage for a resident RHS assigned to an unrealized expression.

entries.tinygrad: Pinned matvec heuristic defaults to MV_BLOCKSIZE=4, MV_THREADS_PER_ROW=8, MV_ROWS_PER_THREAD=4. These originated in 0ba75c437, alongside a Metal matvec benchmark, and carry a TODO to tune by matrix shape.
entries.polygrad: For WEBGPU FP32 only, after the unchanged matvec eligibility test, use 2/16/1 when there is one GLOBAL output axis of at most 1024 elements and a static reduction of at least 256 elements divisible by 16. Otherwise retain the pinned defaults. Setting any MV tile variable disables this default substitution; unspecified knobs keep pinned defaults. WebGPU comparison-enabled BEAM cache identity includes this policy and MV settings.
entries.rationale: More workgroups improve measured small-output kernels. A flat replacement regressed large row-major matrices; even an output<4096 guard regressed N2048/3072. Short reductions also regressed. The narrower rule preserves those schedules. Measurements are from an NVIDIA RTX3060Laptop, not a cross-adapter performance guarantee.
entries.approval: User 2026-10-11 approved investigation followed by a measured size-based update recorded as a divergence, explicitly requiring large LLM shapes before implementation.
entries.close_when: Pinned tinygrad adopts equivalent shape-dependent matvec selection, or broader matched adapter/model evidence supersedes this scoped tile policy. No allowance changes Tensor graphs, values, non-WebGPU default scheduling or explicit tuning settings.

entries.area: bounded symbolic random draws during Model capture
entries.tinygrad: RandMixin.rand rejects symbolic shapes, including bound variables; only concrete nonnegative integer extents are accepted.
entries.polygrad: Model capture may draw floating-point random tensors with positive bounded symbolic extents within one uint32 word chunk. Counts, Threefry split and counter advancement use the actual batch size. Concrete draws retain the pinned path; symbolic draws outside capture, integer random dtypes and oversized draws are rejected with diagnostics.
entries.rationale: Compiled dropout must support partial batches without padding, dropping samples or maintaining an eager fallback. Checkpointed RNG state resumes the same stream.
entries.approval: User 2026-10-12 explicitly approved the scoped Model extension, requiring its own entry, position-sensitive mask checks and diagnostic rejection tests.
entries.close_when: Pinned tinygrad supports the same bounded symbolic random program and actual-size counter progression, or this Model extension is removed. No allowance changes ordinary concrete RNG or compiler rules.

entries.tinygrad: The output-upcast threshold counts static output extents only. Thread admission requires sufficient work at every symbolic binding, even when finite maximum bounds describe much larger workloads.
entries.polygrad: Native CPU and X86 may use finite maximum bounds for output tiling and thread admission. Split axes and divisibility remain static-only; unknown bounds retain the pinned estimate. Fixed-shape scheduling, other backends and symbolic loop extents are unchanged. At runtime, symbolic CPU/X86 calls with positive compute estimates below 128K operations per compiled share execute every share serially on the caller. Missing, unresolved or zero-ALU estimates retain pooled execution: a copy can have zero ALU work but large memory traffic. This launcher policy changes neither kernel code nor share count.
entries.rationale: Preserve output reuse and parallelism for bounded batches without pool wake-up overhead at small actual sizes. Runtime operation estimates and compiler iteration-volume estimates are distinct cost proxies. No padding or partial-tile GEMM is introduced; awkward static dimensions can still be slow.
entries.approval: User 2026-10-12 approved CPU bounded tiling, then maximum-bound thread admission with an actual-work serial fallback within this entry. Freeze further default-heuristic divergences for 0.7.2; GEMM partial tiles, automatic padding and Wasm policy changes are deferred.
entries.close_when: The pinned tinygrad reference adopts equivalent bounded CPU tiling and thread admission, or this compiler policy is removed. No allowance changes dynamic-axis splitting, Tensor graphs or values; caller-versus-pool execution remains a C runtime mechanism.

entries.tinygrad: The v0.14.0 float-decomposition catch-all includes AFTER and casts its storage source, producing an invalid AFTER(CAST(...)) for looped emulated-float accumulators. Upstream commit 6dfca0b79ecfafb4a9f43d34693225c8391e255e (#18278, 2026-09-18) narrows that rule to GroupOp.ALU | {STACK, INDEX}.
entries.polygrad: Backports exactly that operator-set change. Storage and ordering nodes are not arithmetic casts. Native supported dtypes and all other lowering rules are unchanged.
entries.rationale: Fix fixed-size NOOPT max/min reductions and variable-prefix cached attention on emulated dtypes without weakening graph verification or changing model precision.
entries.approval: User 2026-10-13 approved the exact #18278 backport, separate from Qwen3.5, with C/Python/JS regressions and parity checks.
entries.close_when: The pinned reference incorporates 6dfca0b79ecfafb4a9f43d34693225c8391e255e. This allowance does not cover other emulation or reduction-value defects.

entries.area: Upstream X86 address and comparison backports
entries.tinygrad: v0.14 misaddresses narrow unsigned indices, uses unordered float flags for conditional moves and may blend values with a different-width comparison mask.
entries.polygrad: Backports fede35881 (#17787), 6083de5cf (#17801), 38e0fe103 (#17789) and the symmetric half comparison legalization from bc485d271 (#17791). Nonnegative sub-32-bit address indices extend to uint32; float gates materialize boolean masks before flag selection; blend masks match the value dtype.
entries.rationale: Prevent generated-code faults and incorrect NaN and mixed-width selections on the opt-in X86 backend.
entries.approval: User 2026-10-13: proceed with fixes yes, following the reproduced upstream-backport investigation.
entries.close_when: The pin incorporates all four upstream fixes. No other X86 instruction-selection changes are allowed by this entry.

entries.area: Upstream validity, cast-rounding and weak-constant backports
entries.tinygrad: v0.14 applies validity simplification to integer AND, removes ordinary float-half-float rounding and loses movement operations when promoting weak constants.
entries.polygrad: Backports f48b583ee (#17942), 0a8d1c71a (#18294) and the weak-constant promotion and source-width corrections from 0bd725376/f5b00de31 (#17840/#17846). Validity matching is bool-only; cast elision is confined to half-image stores; promotion preserves movement chains and their padding values; weak operations retain every source's required width before narrowing the result.
entries.rationale: Preserve integer graph types, low-precision rounding and padded values. The constant-chain uniformity proof must not project fractional bounds into the compact integer range cache.
entries.approval: User 2026-10-13: proceed with fixes yes.
entries.close_when: The pin incorporates these upstream corrections. No general algebraic or scheduling divergence is permitted.

entries.tinygrad: v0.14 produces NaNs in infinite log reductions and overflowing ELU-family gradients, loses large-input activation accuracy, gives zero erf/asin gradients at zero, overflows low-precision max tie counts and truncates integer-input variance squares.
entries.polygrad: Uses final upstream formulas from 0a1bfc9fa, fdb4109f5, e3c4b3d9b, 1c183e6de, 3123f947b, 4c20f1d35/5c3d04446, 65558fef9/ee3cd4096, ab24cc89e, 79c5d2418 and 34eabf657 in the shared C compositions and gradients, with the full-precision SELU defaults from f9d3f00ff. The erf sign-only backport is superseded by PG-DIV-033; existing tanh policy is unchanged.
entries.rationale: Fix confirmed values and gradients in all consumers of the shared core without frontend duplicates. Reviewed graph pairs match the exact upstream formula hunks applied in memory to the pin; mish additionally composes the unchanged, approved PG-DIV-018 tanh.
entries.approval: User 2026-10-13: proceed with fixes yes.
entries.close_when: The pin incorporates the listed final upstream formulas. No unrelated activation, precision or gradient change is covered.

entries.tinygrad: v0.14 can lose pending writes through realized strided/reshape views, mislabels a nonfinal einsum diagonal, and divides by zero for align-corners interpolation to one element.
entries.polygrad: Backports 593aa1e17/4de13672b view-anchor selection using live C Tensor roots, 1d5d77a15 einsum axis ordering, 26c4b6319 interpolation denominator handling and 2eacd4fa6 matching dilation/kernel axis order for Conv2d same padding. Preserves paired logical/physical roots and the existing assignment publication mechanism.
entries.rationale: Make lazy writes visible to the owning Tensor and preserve requested output shapes and values.
entries.approval: User 2026-10-13: proceed with fixes yes.
entries.close_when: The pin incorporates the listed fixes. This is not permission to change unrelated mutation ownership or symbolic-shape semantics.

entries.tinygrad: Tensor.uop already contains occurrence-specific executable placement when realization begins
entries.polygrad: Default realization consumes the eagerly constructed physical graph directly; explicit placement starts from logical roots plus exact named resource bindings and never consumes a prior physical graph
entries.rationale: Path B removed placement and logical fallback from default realization. The legacy Tensor physicalizer, logical-and-device memo, and runtime-residency AUTO inference are deleted; incomplete raw physical roots fail before callify.

resolution.evidence: Default physical topology, occurrence, mutation, rebuilt-subexpression, JIT, Model, and broad frontend/backend gates pass without realization-time placement or logical-key correspondence. Explicit aggregate place starts from logical roots and exact resource bindings; raw scheduling rejects device-free storage regardless of attached residency.

entries.area: Upstream low-precision extrema, emulation and accumulation backports
entries.tinygrad: v0.14 uses infinite MAX identities for finite-only FP8 formats and emulates FP8 through half when available, losing small e5m2fnuz normals.
entries.polygrad: Backports 99fc6102d finite FP8 extrema, 988651638 float32 FP8 emulation and 6de721f1e float32 accumulation for low-precision floating arange. FNUZ underflow clears the sign exactly as in the pin; this latter correction repairs a porting error, not a divergence.
entries.rationale: Keep reduction, pooling, scatter, sort and symbolic bounds consistent with the finite FP8 dtype range; preserve normal FP8 values without an intermediate half conversion; round arange only after float32 accumulation.
entries.approval: User 2026-10-13 approved upstream bug fixes and requested investigation of both FP8 commits before committing.
entries.close_when: The pin incorporates the three upstream fixes. No other emulated floating-point conversion or accumulation change is permitted.

entries.tinygrad: Variables are PARAM(STACK(), ParamArg(slot=-1, name, vmin_vmax, AddrSpace.ALU))
entries.polygrad: Variables use BUFFER/PARAM with ParamArg AddrSpace.ALU; binding uses AFTER(variable, STORE(variable, value))
entries.rationale: This is shared IR vocabulary debt, not an approved divergence.

resolution.evidence: Removed DEFINE_VAR/BIND and their argument carrier from the C IR, serialization, symbolic passes, scheduler, rangeify, renderers, and tests. Exact symbolic, callify, runtime scalar, and JIT regressions use current BUFFER/PARAM/AFTER+STORE topology.

entries.tinygrad: BUFFER with ParamArg addrspace REG or LOCAL represents compiler storage
entries.polygrad: BUFFER with ParamArg addrspace REG or LOCAL represents compiler storage
entries.rationale: Historical vocabulary debt is closed; resolved rows preserve the audit trail.

resolution.evidence: Removed DEFINE_LOCAL/DEFINE_REG from the C op enum, renderers, interpreter, compiler helpers, and tests; current BUFFER(REG/LOCAL) remains.

entries.tinygrad: Vector constants are STACKs of scalar CONST sources
entries.polygrad: Vector constants use STACKs of scalar CONST sources
entries.rationale: This is shared IR topology debt.

resolution.evidence: Removed VCONST from the C IR, symbolic passes, placement, Model validation, codegen, renderers, and tests; current vector constants use STACK(CONST, ...).

entries.tinygrad: Storage views retain exact SHRINK/BITCAST UOps while Buffer.view owns base/offset runtime state
entries.polygrad: Exact SHRINK/BITCAST UOps now key the same non-owning runtime view metadata
entries.rationale: This is shared storage/view vocabulary debt; it is not the approved deviceless logical graph divergence.

resolution.evidence: Removed the synthetic UOp and constructor; callification retains exact movement UOps while ctx buffer metadata owns aliases.

entries.tinygrad: Tensor graphs use REDUCE with axes encoded in the UOp argument
entries.polygrad: All reduction construction and import use REDUCE with (op, num_axes); REDUCE_AXIS is deleted
entries.rationale: The extra enum is not an approved permanent shared-IR divergence.

resolution.evidence: REDUCE_AXIS and its separate argument carrier were removed from enum, UOp identity, shape inference, symbolic ordering, rendering, IR, realization, and tests; current REDUCE topology gates pass.

entries.tinygrad: RESHAPE/EXPAND use shape-value sources, PAD/SHRINK use start/size shape-value sources, PERMUTE keeps its permutation tuple, and FLIP keeps a rank-sized boolean-mask tuple
entries.polygrad: Tensor construction now uses the same source and argument topology for RESHAPE, EXPAND, PAD, SHRINK, PERMUTE, and FLIP
entries.rationale: This was shared Tensor IR topology debt and was closed by the movement-vocabulary port.

resolution.evidence: Exact tensor-stage PAD/SHRINK/PERMUTE/FLIP corpus passed with zero findings; native, Python, JS native, and JS WASM gates passed.

entries.tinygrad: GETADDR is HCQ2-runtime IR: UOp.getaddr constructs it, spec_hcq accepts direct BUFFER/PARAM sources, and runtime/support/hcq2.py resolves addresses and views. v0.14.0 removed the unused WAIT opcode.
entries.polygrad: GETADDR is absent; the current CUDA/HIP runtimes execute direct driver calls rather than Tinygrad's HCQ2 command-graph pipeline. WAIT is absent in both projects at v0.14.0.
entries.rationale: GETADDR requires a dependency-closed HCQ2 runtime port or an explicit backend-scope exclusion. Adding enum-only scaffolding would not close behavioral parity. WAIT ceased to be a vocabulary gap when upstream removed it; no runtime behavior was invented.
entries.close_when: A dependency-closed HCQ2 runtime port constructs, verifies, lowers, and executes GETADDR with pinned address/view probes, or HCQ2 is explicitly excluded from the supported backend architecture and the vocabulary census gains a reviewed scope rule.

entries.tinygrad: Range propagation collects all consumers
entries.polygrad: The consumer map and per-node consumer-range arrays are dynamically sized from the complete topological consumer set.
entries.rationale: The historical fixed cap was removed by the current indexing.py port.

resolution.evidence: Seventeen matching consumers remain fused; a mismatching seventeenth consumer realizes the shared value in both pinned Tinygrad and Polygrad. Both permanent C cases pass.

entries.tinygrad: PCONTIG=1 preserves matching multi-consumer axes, PCONTIG=2 preserves eligible ended axes, and PCONTIG=3 enables cost-gated or partial-local buffer removal.
entries.polygrad: Range propagation and remove_bufferize implement the same three thresholds, including active-range-gated substitution through effects.
entries.rationale: The complete non-default control is covered by exact topology, effect, and runtime-value probes.

resolution.evidence: PCONTIG=1/2/3 topology matches the pinned branches; closed END/effect ranges remain unchanged; PCONTIG=2 double-matmul and multi-gather outputs are byte-identical to Tinygrad.

entries.tinygrad: Changed EXPAND ranges add the symbolic guarded ranges closure to ending ranges
entries.polygrad: EXPAND passes its injected output-range prefix through poly_uop_ranges and adds every reachable RANGE to ending ranges.
entries.rationale: The historical raw-value append was replaced by the current indexing.py reachable-range closure.

resolution.evidence: The current source expressions match: Tinygrad uses SINK(prefix).ranges and Polygrad uses poly_uop_ranges over each prefix expression. The permanent default-PCONTIG EXPAND ending-range test passes.

entries.tinygrad: WINO=1 selects the implemented Winograd 3x3 convolution path
entries.polygrad: WINO=0 is accepted; nonzero Python Context or environment requests raise NotImplementedError because no core Winograd implementation exists.
entries.rationale: Explicit rejection removes silent no-op configuration, not the missing Winograd capability. This remains open debt, not a parity allowance.
entries.close_when: WINO=0 and WINO=1 source/probe behavior is parity-aligned across required frontends/backends.

entries.tinygrad: Device strings distinguish instances such as CUDA:0 and CUDA:1
entries.polygrad: Core graph metadata retains exact device names/tuples, but frontend/backend admission still excludes genuine same-backend multi-device execution. Public Tensor.shard is absent, including the repeated-device tuple used by test_realize_is_realize.test_multi; that failure occurs before execution and is not a demonstrated multi-GPU failure. UNSHARD has shape/dtype support but no core backward rule.
entries.rationale: Metadata representation and cache separation do not prove multi-device placement or sharded backward execution.
entries.close_when: Device identity is backend plus instance and multi-device construction/lowering passes.

entries.tinygrad: Current bounded HLB-style train comparator captures 20 LINEAR CALLs
entries.polygrad: The same comparator now captures 20 LINEAR CALLs
entries.rationale: The former four-call delta came from high-level SUB, EXP/LOG, reduction accumulation, and softmax/log-softmax topology rather than optimizer or Rangeify behavior. C-owned construction now follows pinned tinygrad and closes the bounded schedule mismatch.

resolution.evidence: The permanent graph oracle passes 69/69 with zero suppressions; isolated model backward is 8/8 CALLs and bounded HLB train/eval/eval-EMA/EMA is 20/8/8/3 in both engines with maximum value error 5.96046448e-08.

entries.tinygrad: Assignment is AFTER(target, STORE(target, value)); current Ops has no ASSIGN member
entries.polygrad: All assignment construction uses AFTER(target, STORE(target, value)); ASSIGN is deleted
entries.rationale: Two live spellings for the same mutation semantics prevent exact graph parity and make the moved/view mutation gate ambiguous.

resolution.evidence: ASSIGN was removed from shared IR, autograd, placement, rangeify, realization, serialization, and raw tests; mutation gates use AFTER/STORE.

entries.tinygrad: Current Ops has no ENCDEC member
entries.polygrad: ENCDEC is absent from the op vocabulary and compiler paths
entries.rationale: Near-dead vocabulary must be proved unreachable and removed or registered as an approved product boundary; silence is not parity.

resolution.evidence: ENCDEC and its rangeify/schedule guards were deleted; the runtime op census no longer reports it.

entries.tinygrad: Current Ops has no INVALID member and cannot construct or import it as a UOp
entries.polygrad: Enum slot zero has no public name and PGIR rejects it before UOp construction
entries.rationale: An internal sentinel must not be accepted as public graph vocabulary.

resolution.evidence: poly_op_name(0) returns no public op and current-version PGIR with op zero is rejected before construction.

entries.area: unsigned maximum constants and scatter amin
entries.tinygrad: Unsigned inverse/minimum use an exact positive dtype.max CONST and scatter amin reduces with inverse/MAX/inverse
entries.polygrad: Unsigned inverse/minimum use the exact positive dtype.max argument, and scatter amin reduces with the same inverse/MAX/inverse topology and zero-sensitive values
entries.rationale: The exact integer carrier closes both the graph-argument debt and the reachable unsigned scatter-amin value bug without a dtype-local surrogate.

resolution.evidence: Unsigned minimum has zero graph findings for uint8/16/32/64. Scatter amin contains the exact positive maximum and inverse/MAX/inverse reducer, has no unary NEG, and returns [[0,100]] for every width.

entries.tinygrad: Numeric host values are staged as numeric source values and converted to the requested dtype in the Tensor graph
entries.polygrad: JavaScript numeric arrays are rounded to exact binary16 storage bits before the shared C host Tensor constructor; the physical graph contains no CAST
entries.rationale: The former route corrupted input before elementwise execution; operations must not compensate for invalid host staging.

resolution.evidence: Direct Array, nested Array, Float64Array, Uint16Array-as-numeric, scalar, non-finite, maximum-finite, and minimum-subnormal cases pass with zero CAST nodes across JS native and Wasm. Browser auto/interpreter/WebGPU use the same constructor regression. The source was implemented in 40c52aa9; the open register row was stale.

entries.tinygrad: Non-truncating symbolic constant folding stores arbitrary-precision Python integers in CONST args, including results above INT64_MAX
entries.polygrad: PolyArg stores canonical exact signed integers outside int64 as immutable base-2^32 magnitudes; symbolic folding keeps Python-style exact results and fixed-width renderers truncate only at their backend boundary
entries.rationale: This closes the former carrier debt with the same semantic boundary as tinygrad rather than suppressing or locally special-casing high-bit constants.

resolution.evidence: Direct, associative, distributive, unary, ternary, weakint-vector, high-bit chained-shift, and large-divisor graphs match pinned tinygrad. Exact C/interpreter, WebGPU long decomposition, CUDA render/runtime, Wasm runtime, IR-v4 round-trip, RNG, and float64x2 SIN gates pass; the full ASan/UBSan/LSan native matrix is 1422/1422.

entries.tinygrad: _pre_scatter constructs shrink, unsqueeze/expand/transpose, one-hot, and pad_to graphs with three retained PAD nodes in the focused rank-two case
entries.polygrad: Scatter uses the shared one-hot helper, retains split dimensions through masked merge, implements no-hit detection as any/logical_not/where, preserves weak Python scalar identities, and crosses the public reduction dtype boundary
entries.rationale: The former whole-graph construction mismatch was a stale duplicate implementation, not an approved divergence.

resolution.evidence: Basic, generalized, include-self, no-self, and all five reducer construction cases match pinned Tinygrad 12/12 with zero allowed or unregistered findings. The complete physical graph corpus is 290/290 exact; C scatter value and occurrence tests are 4/4.

entries.tinygrad: UOp.contiguous returns the original UOp when device is None
entries.polygrad: poly_uop_contiguous and Tensor.contiguous preserve the pinned fold for physical and genuinely storage-free graphs. Portable BUFFER(UNIQUE) materialization is retained under PG-DIV-002; genuine rangeify-created device-free STAGE nodes inherit the physical sink device.
entries.rationale: The legacy raw CONTIGUOUS barrier is removed without restoring implicit realization-time placement. A portable storage graph is not a storage-free expression: the October 4 sort Model regression requires its requested barriers to survive until explicit placement.

resolution.evidence: Raw and Tensor contiguous construction fold device-free values identically. Exact physical graph parity is 278/278; leak-enabled native, Python, JS native/Wasm, rangeify localization, and real CUDA common/specific gates pass.

entries.tinygrad: Python source tuples have no uint16 ceiling; pm_add_control_flow can append a predecessor to a 65,535-source RANGE and produce 65,536 sources
entries.polygrad: PolyUOp.n_src is uint16_t; poly_apply_control_flow and precompiled AFTER accumulation fail cleanly at the ceiling. Optional GROUP/SINK flattening declines an unrepresentable result before count overflow, preserving the original graph.
entries.rationale: The existing C representation cannot encode the pinned result. Clean failure is required for correctness but is not approval of the parity debt or permission to widen the UOp representation implicitly.
entries.close_when: A separately approved arity representation migration carries every UOp/CSE/IR/ABI consumer beyond uint16 and the 65,536-source result matches pinned tinygrad, or the accepted public graph contract explicitly rejects the input before construction.

entries.tinygrad: PYLITERAL carries immutable Python literals used by compiled UPat CUSTOM predicates; v0.14.0 classifies its inferred dtype as void
entries.polygrad: The C pattern compiler has no PYLITERAL UOp or equivalent current compiled-UPat topology
entries.rationale: This is August pattern/compiler vocabulary debt, not an approved semantic divergence.
entries.close_when: The dependency-closed UPat/SPEC migration either ports PYLITERAL with exact compiled-pattern topology or proves the C representation uses the same semantics without exposing a different shared UOp vocabulary.

entries.area: configured default dtype propagation into core lowering
entries.tinygrad: With DEFAULT_FLOAT=float64, pm_lower_weak commits a weak float literal to float64 beneath its weak cast
entries.polygrad: The C-owned default policy reaches weak lowering, storage commitment, promotion, compiler keys and Python/JS. The completed consumer inventory covers indexed-write, embedding, raw loss/mean, QR and seeded factories; explicitly typed RNG, accumulation and Model-family storage retain their existing precision policies.
entries.rationale: The original lowering defect and default-sensitive consumer omissions are fixed and verified with non-default exact graphs and frontend execution. This resolution grants no graph allowance and does not close the exhaustive source-migration wave.
entries.close_when: Carry supported default-dtype configuration through the existing dtype/core owners, inventory related strong-dtype and promotion consumers, and verify non-default exact lowering plus frontend execution. Do not add a weak-lowering-only environment override.

resolution.evidence: Consumer inventory complete; 569 exact graph cases pass without allowances, including 60 non-default controls. Native sanitizers, Python, Node, Wasm and browser checks pass with fixture/capability skips reported separately. Both final paired upstream reports have no execution errors or passing-test regressions. See the source-bound batch index for commands and artifact boundaries.

entries.tinygrad: CHECK_OOB enables uop/spec.py validate_index, using interval bounds and optional Z3 validation for final memory indices
entries.polygrad: C validates index types/shapes but has no equivalent bounds verifier; Python accepts CHECK_OOB=0 and rejects nonzero values explicitly
entries.rationale: A disabled configuration must remain usable without falsely advertising enabled compiler verification. Tensor indexing admission is a separate contract.
entries.close_when: Port optional final-index bounds validation in its core spec owner, compare valid/masked/OOB cases with pinned Tinygrad, and expose only supported configuration. Do not treat the disabled flag or Tensor bounds checks as verifier closure.

entries.tinygrad: fix_group_for_reduce puts the first grouped RANGE axis ID in BufferizeOpts.device; LOCAL device metadata admits an integer identity.
entries.polygrad: PolyArg.bufferize_opts retains the int64 LOCAL identity. Grouped reduction emits the first grouped RANGE ID; argument equality/hash, ordering, diagnostics and PGIR/PGPM preserve it distinctly from absent/string/tuple device metadata.
entries.rationale: The existing BufferizeOpts identity is carried directly, without synthetic device strings or tags. C physical-backend queries do not interpret LOCAL IDs as backend ordinals. Exact construction/CSE and both codec regressions cover the identity; this row grants no allowance.

resolution.evidence: Three observed red regressions now pass: exact grouped STAGE metadata, immutable argument/CSE identity, and integer graph serialization. Both PGIR17/PGPM9 preserve 0, 7, 2^40 and -1; every truncated artifact and old format version is rejected. Owning native suites, CUDA, numerical/physical parity and affected frontends pass. No stage allowance added.

entries.close_when: Represent the integer LOCAL identity through the existing argument, CSE and serialization contracts and test exact STAGE metadata; or obtain an explicit stage-scoped divergence approval supported by consumer analysis.

entries.tinygrad: create_linear_with_vars retains Python integer values without int32 narrowing; the v0.14.0 probe preserves 4294967303 in var_vals
entries.polygrad: ABI80 carries signed64 numeric PolyVarBinding values through scheduling, JIT, CPU/X86/INTERP, CUDA ordinary/graph replay and Wasm. Python and JS reject values outside signed64 before FFI conversion; JS accepts BigInt or safe integer Number. Wider Python integers (including positive uint64 above INT64_MAX) remain unsupported as bindings, independently of typed PARAM bounds. WebGPU retains its supported 32-bit uniform domain.
entries.rationale: The coordinated signed64 runtime transport removes the old int32 narrowing but does not establish arbitrary Python-integer binding parity. No runtime-value limitation is an approved allowance.
evidence: js/test/test_tensor.js:wide scalar bindings preserve BigInt and execute supported values
entries.close_when: Resolve the remaining beyond-signed64 host binding domain, or obtain an explicit stage-scoped release limitation approval with backend admission documented. This row grants no parity allowance.

entries.tinygrad: call_gradient supports precompile, precompile_backward and grad_fxn; precompiled backward can reuse forward outputs as PARAM inputs.
entries.polygrad: FUNCTION forward accepts the precompile flags, but core backward rejects either flag, custom grad_fxn and auxiliary CallInfo. Python function rejects grad_fxn at construction. Tensor custom-kernel callbacks are a separate implemented frontend surface.
entries.rationale: Explicit rejection is not implementation parity or approval to exclude the capability from release claims.
entries.close_when: Port the full backward CallInfo contract with graph and execution controls, or explicitly approve a stage-scoped supported-release limitation.

entries.tinygrad: compute_gradient propagates all_metadata with backward=True onto newly constructed derivative nodes.
entries.polygrad: The C reverse pass has no corresponding per-UOp backward provenance propagation. Program execution metadata is not the same contract.
entries.rationale: Missing diagnostic provenance is separate from numerical gradient correctness; it cannot be counted as equivalent source coverage.
entries.close_when: Implement the pinned diagnostic provenance contract or explicitly approve its omission for the supported release.

entries.area: rank-bounded Tensor and intermediate STAGE shapes
entries.tinygrad: Shapes and _limit_bufs STAGE axes use Python tuples without Polygrad's fixed rank ceiling; the pinned probe constructs a twenty-axis STAGE.
entries.polygrad: POLY_MAX_DIMS is 64. Buffer-limit splitting rejects a replacement needing more than 64 STAGE axes. This is distinct from active RANGE count: flattened coordinates and materialized END nodes retain active dependencies independently of shape rank.
entries.rationale: Preserving complete dependencies does not remove the existing shape representation limit. Explicit rejection is not full parity or an approved release exclusion.
entries.close_when: Remove the rank ceiling through its shape and ABI consumers, or explicitly approve the stage-scoped supported-release limit; never truncate the active RANGE set.

entries.tinygrad: lower_sink_to_linear indexes schedule_cache by function.key bytes; the cache does not retain the source SINK as its key.
entries.polygrad: Ordinary schedule keys now copy a cached recursive SHA256 digest, without retaining the source SINK. The full 32 bytes determine equality; the first 32 bits only index the map. Host gradient callbacks and auxiliary objects unsupported by the shared field encoder retain the pointer-key fallback. LINEAR values remain retained, with no eviction policy or size cap, as in the pin. Explicit poly_schedule_cache_clear releases cache ownership at an idle boundary.
entries.rationale: This is a cache lifetime difference, not a demonstrated numerical mismatch. The September13 split-owner HLB diagnostic releases source keys while retaining every LINEAR value: host arena_bytes falls by 1,740,007 and 2,729 UOps retire, but CUDA bytes remain unchanged. The 593,152 CUDA bytes belong to cache values, not uniquely to keys; replacing keys alone will not reclaim them. The separate 18,352,660-byte post-function delta disappears at collection and is not this debt. No leak beyond context lifetime is established. The October15 eager probe attributes 178,508 of 812,436 tracked graph bytes (22%) to source-key retention; LINEAR values retain the remainder. Replacing pointer keys with the existing uncached canonical encoder projects about 113 KB saved before key wrappers, but measured warm scheduling slows 16-24% and eager calls 4.4%. That rejected prototype re-encodes each lookup, unlike Tinygrad's cached recursive digest; it does not evaluate a faithful cached-key port. The cached-digest port now removes ordinary source-key retention. A matched 32-shape probe reduces schedule-only tracked graph bytes from 812,436 to 642,744 (plus 1,280 bytes of key records). With all compiler caches retained, the eight-byte private field per node raises tracked graph memory from 62.62 to 63.22 MB. This is not a universal memory reduction. Warm scheduling medians increase about 3-4%, while eager-call ranges overlap. The remaining debt is limited to unsupported host-metadata pointer keys; callback lifetime semantics are not changed by this port.
entries.close_when: Establish lifetime-safe identity for host callbacks/auxiliary metadata without retaining their source SINK, with callback ownership and replay regressions; or explicitly approve this remaining fallback. Ordinary graph key retention is fixed. Digest caching does not bound LINEAR or other compiler-cache growth.

entries.tinygrad: Both APIs support data-dependent output lengths and explicit size/fill_value variants usable during JIT capture.
entries.polygrad: The Tensor methods are absent, including fixed-size variants. Three upstream JIT cases stop at AttributeError before testing capture or numerical behavior.
entries.rationale: This is not solely a dynamic-shape scheduler limitation. test_item_bakes_in_values also stops at the missing method before exercising the host-read guard. Registration grants no allowance or passing result.
entries.close_when: Implement the shared Tensor semantics and frontend bindings with fixed-size/JIT and dynamic-size controls, without weakening the capture host-read guard.

entries.tinygrad: TinyJit captures functions using realized closure tensors, including calls with only scalar variable arguments.
entries.polygrad: Python raises JitError: JIT requires at least one Tensor input on capture because the wrapper selects its PolyCtx from Tensor arguments. The C begin-capture API admits zero inputs; the observed restriction is in the frontend.
entries.rationale: The two upstream cases fail explicitly before replay. This is a context-selection capability gap, not evidence of incorrect replay values. Registration does not approve a divergence.
entries.close_when: Define and test context ownership for closure-only/scalar-only Python capture, including mixed-context rejection and replay after closure-state writes.

entries.tinygrad: Tensor slicing/padding accepts symbolic UOp bounds. test_symbolic_pad_view_frozen additionally asserts a known capture bug and a contiguous workaround.
entries.polygrad: The test stops in _pair_array with TypeError: 'UOp' object cannot be interpreted as an integer, before either reference behavior is exercised.
entries.rationale: Python padding still uses the int64 pair adapter; shrink, reshape and expand already have symbolic UOp-backed paths. Do not implement Tinygrad's documented frozen-pad wrong result to make the footgun test pass; use correct-value controls for future support.
entries.close_when: Carry symbolic padding arguments through the frontend with exact graph and changing-bound value tests; separately disposition the reference's known-bug assertion.

entries.tinygrad: Device[Device.DEFAULT].graph exposes its graph runner constructor or None; the CPU control skips test_graph_input_output_aliasing when no graph runner is available.
entries.polygrad: Python Compiled has no graph attribute, so the same test fails at capability inspection rather than executing its alias scenario. C CUDA graph execution is implemented and tested separately.
entries.rationale: Do not fabricate a runner object or turn an absent attribute into evidence of missing CUDA graph execution. This CPU comparison contains no graph execution in either provider.
entries.close_when: Expose truthful graph capability semantics without a fabricated Python GraphRunner, and execute the unchanged alias scenario on a graph-capable provider.

entries.tinygrad: DEV contains Target(device, renderer, arch, interface, indices) requests separated by semicolons; CPU;CUDA can configure both targets while default Tensor construction selects CPU. CUDA:1 is a renderer request, not a device ordinal.
entries.polygrad: Implicit selection accepts one supported backend name or CPU:X86. Other target fields and multiple targets are rejected rather than discarded. Explicit device choices override POLY_DEV, then DEV; POLY_LIB is the Polygrad loader path.
entries.rationale: Recipe compatibility does not imply the full Target selection vocabulary. This is distinct from genuine multi-device execution debt013 and grants no graph or behavioral allowance.
entries.close_when: Port supported multi-target/renderer/interface/architecture selection with matching pinned probes, without treating unimplemented backends as executable or dropping target fields.

entries.tinygrad: CStyleLanguage.render names PARAM values data{slot}_{shape}, including the trailing underscore for scalar shapes.
entries.polygrad: The C-style and WGSL renderers name parameters data{slot}, omitting the shape suffix. Argument numbering and runtime binding remain separate from this diagnostic spelling.
entries.rationale: Source-text parity is incomplete. This is not a demonstrated value or argument-binding defect and grants no graph or numerical allowance. Do not change names to conceal incorrect imported PARAM slots.
entries.close_when: Port the supported renderer naming convention with source comparisons while preserving independent slot, signature and execution assertions.
